attacks.claim: Rollback re-enables MailPoet sending from a snapshot taken before cutover. Unsubscribes and suppressions recorded in Ghost during the 30-day read-only window are not written back to MailPoet, so people who opted out in Ghost could be re-mailed. Re-mailing opted-out subscribers is a compliance violation and cannot be undone.
attacks.evidence: "rollback = repoint DNS and re-enable MailPoet sending, with any new Ghost signups exported and re-imported to MailPoet" (ABSENT: unsubscribe/suppression reverse sync and paid-member/Stripe state reconciliation on rollback)

attacks.claim: The plan has no delta sync between the last MailPoet export and the cutover. Subscribers who joined, unsubscribed, or bounced after the import would be wrong or missing in Ghost. No production import date is given.
attacks.evidence: "Dry-run import on staging in week 1" (ABSENT: production import date and final delta sync)

attacks.claim: Stripe is connected directly to Ghost while the old membership and Stripe plugins may still receive the same webhooks during cutover and the 30-day read-only period. Duplicate or conflicting subscription events could double-grant or cancel memberships. The plan does not say when old plugins are disconnected from Stripe.
attacks.evidence: "Stripe: existing Stripe account connected directly; no change in processor."

attacks.claim: Feed and REST URLs are not covered. RSS readers and any email or third-party links to /feed/ or WP REST endpoints would break at cutover. The 200/301 crawl only covers the 2,000 most-visited pages.
attacks.evidence: "A crawl of the 2,000 most-visited URLs from analytics must return 200/301 before cutover." (ABSENT: /feed/ and RSS redirect plan)

attacks.claim: MailPoet list-level membership cannot map cleanly to Ghost's single newsletter model. The plan exports list membership but never defines how it is mapped, so readers who were on a specific list may be re-subscribed to the wrong content or dropped.
attacks.evidence: "Export MailPoet subscribers with status, list membership, subscribe date" (ABSENT: list-to-Ghost mapping rule)

attacks.claim: The deliverability gate is unsafe. A 2-hour check cannot measure complaint rate, which arrives hours or days later. Sending 46k mail from a Mailgun domain warmed for about one week is also aggressive. The seed segment's selection criteria are not specified. The gate could pass while damage is still accumulating.
attacks.evidence: "if bounce rate < 2% and complaint rate < 0.1%" and "Mailgun domain warm-up (SPF/DKIM/DMARC)" in week 2

attacks.claim: Ghost, MySQL, and bulk-send workers run on the same single VPS, which is the same contention pattern behind the four send-day outages. The plan gives no monitoring, alerting, or send-failure runbook, and the success metric measures outage count rather than detecting failures.
attacks.evidence: "MySQL 8 on the same box" (ABSENT: monitoring, alerting, and send-job isolation)

attacks.claim: Backups are restored only at the export level. No full DB restore from the nightly dumps is tested, and no RPO/RTO is stated. The backup encryption key custody is also undefined, so an unrecoverable key would make the backups useless.
attacks.evidence: "nightly encrypted dumps to object storage (30-day retention)" (ABSENT: full restore test, RPO/RTO, key custody)

attacks.claim: Backup encryption key custody is undefined. Admin hardening, firewalling of MySQL and Ghost admin, and secret handling for Mailgun, Stripe, and object storage credentials are not addressed. The 30-day read-only old VPS keeps full subscriber PII online with no hardening or decommission plan.
attacks.evidence: "nightly encrypted dumps to object storage (30-day retention)" and "WordPress stays running read-only on the old VPS for 30 days" (ABSENT: key custody, admin hardening, secrets handling)

attacks.claim: Consent IP and source data are imported only "where recorded", so some records will lack consent evidence. Importing them into Ghost and retaining them with no retention policy raises personal-data risk. The old VPS also retains PII for 30 days with no stated retention end.
attacks.evidence: "consent source/IP where recorded" (ABSENT: consent-evidence gap handling and retention policy for old-VPS data)

attacks.claim: No legal basis is documented for transferring marketing consent from MailPoet to Ghost. There is no Mailgun DPA or sub-processor disclosure, and no unsubscribe-compliance check covering the list-level opt-outs that will be lost in the mapping.
attacks.evidence: "Mailgun only receives per-send recipient batches." (ABSENT: DPA, consent-transfer basis, sub-processor disclosure)

attacks.claim: Exit path is unproven at scale. The rehearsal uses 50 addresses through a different vendor, not the 46k list, and it does not test a cold-domain sender. Mailgun is a single bulk-send dependency, and the exit cost is not estimated.
attacks.evidence: "rehearse this end to end with a 50-address internal list through Postmark Broadcasts"

attacks.claim: The Mailgun cost ($90/mo) is an estimate with no quote. The 4 vCPU / 8 GB sizing for 46k subscribers and 6,812 posts is unbenchmarked. The shortcode fix script and the /YYYY/MM/slug/ routes.yaml approach are unprototyped in the plan.
attacks.evidence: "Estimated $90/mo at our volume (46k x ~4.3 sends/month)" and "41 posts with embedded shortcodes fixed by script"

attacks.claim: The run-cost line is ambiguous: it is unclear whether Mailgun is included in the ~$140/mo figure. The 30-day double-running of old and new stacks and the Postmark rehearsal costs are not counted in the comparison to $95/mo.
attacks.evidence: "Total run cost: ~$140/mo VPS + Mailgun + storage, vs $95/mo today."

attacks.claim: Bulk-send volume and email-log/analytics growth in the co-located MySQL have no retention or capacity plan. Sending 46k recipients per send is a hot path with no stated load test.
attacks.evidence: "MySQL 8 on the same box" (ABSENT: load test and data-growth retention)

attacks.claim: The newsletter email template is not addressed. Only a site "theme port" is mentioned, so the visual rendering of the weekly send, which is the core product, has no QA plan.
attacks.evidence: "theme port" (ABSENT: email template design and render QA)

attacks.claim: Nothing material: the stated goals of reliable publishing and owned reader relationships match the plan's scope.
attacks.evidence: "Mission: publish reliably and keep reader relationships owned by the publication"

attacks.claim: Domain cutover can break existing member sign-in sessions and links, causing extra steps for readers, with no mention of session or magic-link handling.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: member session and sign-in link behavior across the domain cutover

attacks.claim: No accessibility acceptance criteria exist for the ported theme or the new email template.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: accessibility criteria for theme port and email template

attacks.claim: Scope is over-allocated for 0.5 FTE over four weeks. The work includes VPS build, Ghost, theme port, Mailgun warm-up, Stripe import, redirects, scripted shortcode fixes, 37 manual reconciliations, and a Postmark rehearsal. No owner is named for the go/no-go decision.
attacks.evidence: "Owner: dev (0.5 FTE) + managing editor | 4 weeks"
